newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee nuclear plant off-line for months.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee nuclear plant off-line for months.

text.p: The Maine Yankee nuclear power plant is unlikely to resume operations in mid-March as plant officials had originally planned, a spokeswoman warned Thursday.
Plant officials expect the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to impose new conditions on the 910-megawatt plant that will again delay its returning to operation, spokeswoman Maureen Brown said.
"Maine Yankee expects to remain off-line for several more months." Brown said. The plant in Wiscasset has been off-line since Dec. 6 while engineers fix misrouted electrical cables.
Brown said company officials still hope to complete what she called a "very, very complex" repair operation by mid-March "but it may well take longer."
The NRC told Maine Yankee it had been placed on the list because regulators had discovered "a number of significant weaknesses in equipment monitoring, testing, engineering and licensing."
Brown said the delay was not a direct result of the NRC's Wednesday announcement that Maine Yankee was on its Watch List of problem nuclear facilities needing increased scrutiny.
She said she expected new operating conditions to be imposed by the NRC in connection with problems discovered during a special Independent Safety Assessment conducted on the facility last summer.

NRC Chairman Shirley Jackson said last week she expects Maine Yankee will be fined because of the problems that were uncovered. Maine Yankee officials are to meet with NRC staff Feb. 4 to discuss the plant's response to that special reveiw.

Maine Yankee's directors have signed a tentative agreement with Entergy Corp to take over management operations of the 24-year-old facility. That agreement is expected to be completed in early February, Brown said.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co. and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
